scope: Theorem 1.1 (The unrestricted low-corank Selmer converse) of the manuscript “The Selmer converse for elliptic curves at every prime” (preprints/The-Selmer-converse-for-elliptic-curves-at-every-prime-October-7-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 002 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 bdb2f21b345a4f0f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every elliptic curve A0/Q, every prime p, and r ∈ {0, 1}, sp(A0) = r =⇒ a(A0) = rankZ A0(Q) = r, # Sha(A0/Q) < ∞. There is no restriction on reduction type, complex multiplication, the residual representation, rational torsion, or rational isogenies.
